setup_name: ADR vs home-market earnings dislocation (cross-border arb)
instrument: US-listed ADRs of Japanese stocks vs Tokyo shares, USD/JPY hedge
time_of_day: US session after a Tokyo-close news event; exit at Tokyo open
universe_filter: ~50 dual-listed Japanese names (e.g. Sony, Honda, NTT); company reports or news after the Tokyo close
conditions: Company releases earnings/news after Tokyo close
ADR in New York moves X% vs Tokyo close (FX-adjusted)
Trader judges the NY reaction too small or too large given the news and past earnings reactions
entry_trigger: Buy (or short) the ADR in New York when its move looks mispriced versus how Tokyo will open; hedge the yen exposure
stop: None mechanical; risk is the Tokyo open gap (limit-up/limit-down can trap the position)
target_or_exit: Unwind against the Tokyo shares at the Tokyo open
management: Often run delta neutral (long one name, short another) so FX legs net out
stated_edge: Algorithms price ADRs well on quiet days off Nikkei futures, S&P futures and USD/JPY, but misprice earnings and high-volatility events; a specialist who reads the numbers judges the reaction better
data_needed: Foreign-market prices, ADR ratios, FX, news/earnings text, ability to collapse cross-border trades
mcf_translation: Not mappable to MCF's US 5-min bar lab. Closest analog: US stocks that reprice on overnight news vs futures-implied open (gap fade/extension study).

setup_name: Crisis-day beta pair: short high-beta, long defensive
universe_filter: Pairs of names in the same market, one high-beta (e.g. auto maker) and one defensive (e.g. telecom), both down similar amounts
conditions: Index futures down sharply (about 3%)
High-beta and low-beta names show similar % drops in the US session
entry_trigger: Short the high-beta name, buy the defensive name in equal dollar amounts
stop: Not stated
target_or_exit: Close when the home market opens and the beta gap re-asserts
management: Dollar-neutral pair
stated_edge: During forced liquidation, prices move in lockstep; on the next open the high-beta name falls far more than the defensive one
stated_stats: One cited example: high-beta name fell ~15% vs ~2% for the defensive name
data_needed: Beta estimates (computable from daily bars); historical crisis days are few
mcf_translation: On days SPY gap/close down > 2.5%, find pairs within a sector where daily-bar beta differs a lot but same-day returns are within 1%; long low-beta / short high-beta at close, exit next close; measure spread return.

setup_name: Absorption fade at a price that buyers/sellers cannot get through
instrument: futures (10-yr note, 5-yr note, T-bond, ultra bond; also ES)
time_of_day: first 2-3 hours after the open; more trades on high-news days (e.g. payrolls)
universe_filter: Deep, liquid futures order books; avoid thin books (crude, gold, DAX) for discretionary scalping
conditions: Market grinds toward a price level
Repeated hits at the level fail to trade through; large traded volume at the level without price progress
Fresh resting size reloads at the level
entry_trigger: Join the side that is holding the level (e.g. short against the level that buyers cannot lift), placing a limit order where possible
stop: 1-2 ticks beyond the level for a fade; if price is 2 ticks against and new sellers do not quickly push it back to entry, exit; emergency stop-market 3-5 ticks away
target_or_exit: 2-6 ticks typical; exit manually when order flow shows the move stalling rather than relying on a trailing stop
management: All-in/all-out sizing; re-enter if exited too early; scratch at break-even if no follow-through; hold 2-12 min typically
stated_edge: Prices move only when market orders overwhelm resting liquidity; watching traded volume at each price shows where real interest defends a level
stated_stats: 3-10 trades on a typical day, up to ~20-25 on volatile days; targets shrank from 12-14 to 4-7 ticks after HFT
data_needed: Level 2 / depth of market, tick-level trades with aggressor side, futures data
mcf_translation: Crude proxy only: on 5-min bars, a level touched 3+ times with high volume and no close beyond it -> fade with stop just beyond the level. Real signal needs order book.

setup_name: Inside-market size imbalance: lean with the heavy side
universe_filter: Liquid futures with deep books
conditions: Inside bid size far exceeds inside offer size (e.g. ~10:1) or vice versa
Aggressive market orders are sweeping successive levels on one side
entry_trigger: If wanting to sell when the bid is much larger, rest a sell limit on the thin offer (likely to fill); if buying in that case, take the offer with a market order. When market orders wipe out several bid levels, go with the sellers or stand aside
stop: Typically 1-4 ticks depending on context
target_or_exit: A few ticks, until the book evens out
management: Scratch trades that do not move quickly
stated_edge: Heavy one-sided interest tends to keep trades printing on the thin side until the book rebalances
data_needed: Level 2 book sizes, tick data
mcf_translation: Not mappable to 5-min bars.

setup_name: SPY RSI(2) mean reversion (daily)
universe_filter: SPY (or other ETFs classified as mean-reverting on the daily interval)
conditions: 2-period RSI on daily closes falls below 30
entry_trigger: Buy when RSI(2) < 30
stop: None (guest argues stops cut mean-reversion trades before they revert)
target_or_exit: Sell when RSI(2) > 70
management: Fixed ~15% of account per position across ~7 algos; no leverage
stated_edge: SPY has shown daily mean reversion since roughly the 1980s-90s (earlier it showed momentum); oversold dips tend to bounce
stated_stats: Guest recalls Sharpe above 1 over 10-15 years and smaller 2008 drawdown than buy-and-hold (not precise)
mcf_translation: Daily bars: RSI(2) on SPY close; long at close when RSI2<30, exit at close when RSI2>70; also test 5-min version on liquid ETFs as an intraday analog (RSI(2) on 5-min closes, flat by close).

setup_name: RSI momentum (buy overbought, sell oversold) on momentum-regime assets
instrument: ETFs/ETNs (GDXJ intraday, HYG 2-hour, inverse-vol ETNs XIV/SVXY)
universe_filter: Assets the regime scan classifies as momentum-persistent on that bar interval
conditions: Asset/interval classified as momentum (see regime-scan setup)
RSI moves into overbought zone
entry_trigger: Buy when RSI crosses into overbought (exact mirror of mean-reversion rule); short GDXJ when RSI goes oversold
stop: Indicator-based exit; fixed stops/targets only on weaker-anomaly assets
target_or_exit: Exit when RSI drops to oversold (or opposite threshold)
management: 15% of account per trade, ~4-5 assets at a time
stated_edge: Some assets show persistent trend behaviour at specific bar intervals; using a momentum rule on them and avoiding them for mean reversion
stated_stats: Combined 7-algo backtest claims 60-70%/yr; live ~17% YTD with Sharpe ~2 over ~15 months (heavily driven by inverse-vol products)
mcf_translation: For each ETF in MCF universe and each bar size (5-min, 30-min, 60-min aggregated, daily), compute returns of RSI(n) momentum rule vs mean-reversion rule; trade the rule that wins in the trailing window. Intraday: RSI(14) on 5-min > 70 -> long, exit < 30, flat at close.

setup_name: Quarterly momentum vs mean-reversion regime scan ('binocular')
time_of_day: run quarterly across 30-min, 1-hour, 2-hour, daily, weekly intervals
universe_filter: All ETFs; ~95% classify as random walk and are skipped
conditions: For each asset x bar interval, measure expected return of an oscillator-based momentum rule (x-axis) and mean-reversion rule (y-axis)
Classify into momentum, mean-reversion or random-walk quadrant
Pick 4-5 assets with the strongest anomaly / best risk-reward
entry_trigger: Selection only; trades come from simple 2-5 parameter rules matched to the regime
stop: n/a
target_or_exit: Re-scan each quarter
management: Few parameters (<10, usually 5-6) to limit overfitting
stated_edge: The edge is in choosing the asset/timeframe, not the entry rule; most assets are efficient and untradeable
mcf_translation: Walk-forward: each quarter, for every symbol x bar size, compute in-sample expectancy of RSI-momentum and RSI-reversion rules; trade next quarter only symbol/interval pairs above a threshold; must count all symbol x interval x rule combos as configurations tried.

setup_name: Combined-predictor SPY market timing (incl. variance risk premium)
universe_filter: SPY only
conditions: Forecast 6-month-ahead (or 1-month-ahead) S&P excess return by combining ~20 published predictors (dividend/price, P/E, CAPE, variance risk premium = VIX minus realised S&P volatility, etc.)
Map forecast to over/underweight of SPY
entry_trigger: Set SPY exposure proportional to the combined forecast at each rebalance
stop: None
target_or_exit: Rebalance on schedule
management: Leverage up/down around 100% SPY
stated_edge: Many predictors are individually weak out of sample but combining them yields a forecast strong enough to trade; variance risk premium is strongest near a 3-month horizon
stated_stats: Backtest 2001-2015: about twice SPY's average return at half the volatility (~4x Sharpe) - backtest only
data_needed: VIX history, valuation ratios (dividend yield, earnings, CAPE)
mcf_translation: Daily bars give realised vol; need VIX series. Simple test: monthly SPY exposure = f(VIX - 21-day realised vol); higher premium -> higher exposure. Not an intraday setup but could act as a regime filter for intraday long bias.

firm_or_style: prop (Seven Points Capital), discretionary momentum + scalping
setup_name: Descending triangle short in a faded low-cap runner
time_of_day: after the initial run stalls; often midday onward
universe_filter: Low-cap 'trash' names that have run up several hundred percent and started making lower highs
conditions: Stock already up a few hundred percent
Momentum stalls: a lower high forms after a dip
Successive dips and lower highs form a descending triangle over a flat-ish support
entry_trigger: Three possible shorts: (1) inside the triangle near a lower high, (2) on the break of triangle support, (3) on a failed retest of the broken support from below
stop: Above the triangle's last lower high (fixed dollar risk per entry)
target_or_exit: Not specified; trade the breakdown leg
management: Size larger only when the setup is clean; take every valid instance to keep results consistent
stated_edge: Exhausted runners lose buyers; lower highs show supply, and support breaks trigger liquidation
data_needed: Float data; reliable short-locate availability; low-cap universe coverage in MCF
mcf_translation: Universe: stocks with close >= 3x price of 5 sessions ago (or intraday gain > 100%). On 5-min bars, detect >= 2 lower swing highs with roughly flat swing lows (tolerance 1-2%); short on 5-min close below the flat low; stop above last swing high; exit at close or at 2R.

setup_name: Join the trend on a pullback into support
instrument: US stocks (large caps with catalysts, e.g. INTC/AAPL on news)
universe_filter: Names in play with fresh news/catalyst; gappers; scanner on volume, range, volatility, float
conditions: Stock trending up on a catalyst
Pulls back into a support level (prior breakout level / high-volume node on volume profile)
Volume and tape show sellers drying up at support
entry_trigger: Buy at support with a tight stop, sizing up because risk is small
stop: Just below support (where the pattern is invalidated)
target_or_exit: Ride the trend; if green by end of day, hold as a swing per exit rules
management: Fixed dollar risk per trade; scale in/out across prices; best trades work immediately
stated_edge: Pullbacks within established trends at high-volume support offer low risk relative to continuation
stated_stats: Guest reports green every month for ~3 years trading ~15 setups and ~50M shares/month (overall, not per setup)
data_needed: News/catalyst flag would improve filtering
mcf_translation: Stocks with gap > 3% and rvol > 2; trend = price above VWAP and rising 20-EMA on 5-min; entry when price pulls back to VWAP or prior-day high/opening-range high and the 5-min bar closes back above it; stop below the pullback low; exit at close (or hold overnight if day closes green above VWAP).

setup_name: Range scalping ('market making') in liquid low-priced stocks
horizon: scalp (<5 min) to intraday (up to ~1 hour)
universe_filter: Price $5-20, at least ~10M shares/day, daily range ~20-50 cents (e.g. AMD at the time)
conditions: Deep liquidity so size can be bought/sold without moving price
Stock oscillating within an intraday range
entry_trigger: Buy near the low end of the range / sell near the high end, posting or taking liquidity as needed
stop: Scratch quickly if price moves through the level
target_or_exit: Capture a piece of the intraday range
management: Trade size; relies on low/no commissions and rebates
stated_edge: Mean reversion inside the range plus near-zero execution costs at a prop firm
stated_stats: Share of firm P&L has declined vs momentum trading in recent years
data_needed: Tick/quote data; realistic per-share costs; MCF retail cost assumptions likely kill the edge
mcf_translation: Low priority: on 5-min bars for $5-20 stocks with ADV > 10M, fade touches of the morning range high/low back toward VWAP; must include full costs since the stated edge depends on near-zero fees.

firm_or_style: retail full-time day trader, long-biased small caps
setup_name: Intraday bull flag / pennant breakout in high-rvol sub-$10 stocks
time_of_day: from the open; first breakouts after an initial push
universe_filter: Price < $10; volume >= 2.5x average daily volume (Finviz scan); ranked A/B/C by chart, sector theme, low float, high short interest
conditions: Stock makes a strong move to a high of day
Pulls back / consolidates in a tight flag or pennant (3-min chart)
Price holding above VWAP
Daily and 1-hour charts not blocked by nearby resistance (check 20-day support/resistance, 50/200-day MAs)
entry_trigger: Buy the break above the consolidation high (never the first breakout of the day; wait for consolidation)
stop: Tight: just below the consolidation; exit fully at a scratch/small loss if the breakout fails
target_or_exit: Sell a first partial immediately into the breakout pop; scale out on the way up; final target at a daily level such as the 200-day MA; ~1/5 of size left by final target
management: Full size in one entry ('one bullet'), then take risk off right away; scale out if volume absorbs at a level without price progress
stated_edge: High relative volume means many participants watch the same levels; flags after a strong push break with follow-through; quick partials avoid failed-breakout losses
stated_stats: Reported ~1400% compounded return in 2017 with small drawdowns; one red day in the early part of the next year (self-reported, bull/crypto-mania period)
data_needed: Float and short interest optional; 3-min bars (MCF has 5-min)
mcf_translation: Universe: price < $10, rvol >= 2.5 by 10:00. On 5-min bars after a >= 5% push from open, detect 3-6 bar consolidation with range < 40% of the push and lows above VWAP; buy on break of consolidation high; stop below consolidation low; sell 1/3 at +1R, 1/3 at +2R, rest at close or VWAP loss.

setup_name: Hot-sector leader long when peers turn green
instrument: US stocks (theme/sector momentum names, e.g. blockchain names in Dec 2017)
universe_filter: 4-5 stocks in a speculative theme moving 50-100% daily; trade the leaders, not laggards
conditions: Theme is in a risk-on mania with heavy volume
Names open weak / red
One or two peers turn green on the day
entry_trigger: Buy the sector leader as peers flip green, using peers as leading indicators
stop: Below intraday low / VWAP (not specified exactly)
target_or_exit: Hold longer than a normal scalp while the theme is hot; stop pressing when friends/family start asking about the theme (crowding)
management: Bigger size while liquidity is deep; back off as the move gets extended
stated_edge: Correlated theme names move together; leaders outperform laggards
stated_stats: December 2017 was the guest's best month (more than first 5 months combined)
data_needed: Theme/sector groupings for small caps; news/catalyst tags
mcf_translation: Define groups (by sector code or user list). When >= 2 of group members cross from red to green vs prior close after opening down, buy the group member with the highest 5-day return on its own cross of prior close; stop below day low; exit at close.

firm_or_style: independent full-time short seller of small caps
setup_name: Backside short of a parabolic low-float hype runner
instrument: US stocks (low float, often < 5M shares, low priced)
time_of_day: any; often after day 3 of a parabolic run
universe_filter: Low-float stocks up several hundred to 1000%+ over days/weeks on news that does not justify the move (hype/manipulation; e.g. crypto/blockchain or MoviePass-type pivots); need short locates
conditions: Multi-day or multi-week run (the bigger the run, the higher the conviction)
Run is parabolic; often day 3+ of the parabolic leg
Exhaustion: big drop on heavy volume and/or failed bounce below a prior high (the 'backside')
entry_trigger: Starter short (e.g. 5-10k shares) at a failed bounce / breakdown; add only as it moves in your favour (hit the bid on breakdowns); never add to a losing short
stop: Above intraday resistance / high of day; exit if it breaks resistance, especially on volume ('paper cut' losses), then look to re-enter later
target_or_exit: Hold for the 40-70% collapse typical after the peak; may hold overnight or for weeks once on the backside
management: Small size on the front side; full/large size only on backside of multi-week runners; hold little overnight on day-1 runners due to PR/halt risk; several brokers for locates and fees
stated_edge: Hype runners on thin floats nearly always deflate; the 'air' in the price makes risk/reward on the backside very favourable
stated_stats: Guest says these few 'golden' setups (3-6 per year) produce ~75-80% of annual income; claims ~90-95% success on top setups (self-assessed)
data_needed: Float, short borrow availability and fees, halt data; low-cap coverage
mcf_translation: Universe: close >= 3x the close 10 sessions earlier and price > $2. Daily: after first day closing below prior day's low on volume >= 1.5x 10-day avg, short next open; stop above the run's high; exit after N days or at 50% retrace of the run. Intraday variant: on 5-min, short first lower high after a high-volume break of VWAP on a day-3+ runner; stop above HOD; cover at close. Add borrow fees to costs.

firm_or_style: ex-prop (TMG) fixed-income relative value, launching a CTA
setup_name: Treasury cash vs futures relative-value spread
instrument: US Treasury cash notes vs CME Treasury futures
universe_filter: On-the-run 5-30 year Treasuries and matching futures
conditions: Spread between cash bond and future deviates from its historical relationship given the rate regime (curve steepening/flattening)
entry_trigger: Long the cheap leg / short the rich leg when the model says over- or under-valued; execution is automated
stop: Pre-set risk parameters per contract volatility
target_or_exit: Spread returns toward historical norm
management: Size cut when risk at the planned entry is too large; trade less in erratic regimes
stated_edge: Historical relationships between related rate instruments tend to persist; discretion on regime plus systematic execution
data_needed: Treasury cash and futures prices, carry/repo data
mcf_translation: Not mappable to MCF stock lab; conceptually similar to ETF pair spreads (e.g. IEF vs TLT) on daily bars.

setup_name: Bear-market rule: sell rallies, never sell big down days
universe_filter: Index in a confirmed bear regime (example: Nasdaq holds below a key level for about a month)
conditions: Bear regime confirmed
Market has a sharp rally / pop up toward resistance
entry_trigger: Short into the rally (or buy puts on the pop); on big down days buy near-the-money calls and short ~1.5 futures per call for defined-risk short exposure
stop: Defined by option premium / structure
target_or_exit: Not specified
management: Never initiate shorts after a large down day, to avoid 50-70 point short-covering rips
stated_edge: Bear markets do not fall in a straight line; violent rallies punish shorts added after big declines
data_needed: Options for the structured version
mcf_translation: Daily SPY/QQQ: regime = close below 200-day MA for 20+ sessions. Short only after a 2-day rally of >= 2% (or close above 10-day MA), exit after N days or on new low; compare to shorting after down days >= 2%. Could serve as a direction/timing filter for intraday short setups in bear regimes.

firm_or_style: independent ex-floor spread trader (Sydney Futures Exchange)
setup_name: 'Price spread divergence': spread fails to confirm a new high in the outright
instrument: interest-rate futures spreads (AU 3-yr vs 10-yr bonds, bank bills); concept portable to related ETF pairs
universe_filter: Pairs whose spread normally trends with the outright market (e.g. curve narrows as bonds rally because the 10-yr is more volatile)
conditions: Outright market makes successive new highs while the spread makes successive new lows (normal co-movement)
Market makes a new high (or retests the old high) but the spread does NOT make a new low (divergence)
entry_trigger: Put on the spread in the opposite direction to its trend (e.g. buy the curve) at the divergence
stop: Guest uses no stops; manages via spread structure and size
target_or_exit: Spread reverting toward prior levels; trade works whether outright rises or falls
management: Discretionary; position reviewed against charts after the close
stated_edge: The leg that led the move is losing sponsorship; the spread reverses before the outright does, and the spread position is largely neutral to market direction
data_needed: Futures data for the original; for stocks need suitable high-beta/low-beta ETF pairs
mcf_translation: Analog on ETFs: spread = log(QQQ) - beta*log(SPY) (or a sector ETF vs SPY). Normally spread rises with SPY new highs; when SPY makes a 20-day high on 5-min/daily bars but the spread is below its own value at the prior SPY high, short the spread (short QQQ / long beta-weighted SPY); exit after N days or when the spread makes a new low/high.

setup_name: Short company-breaking bad news in an illiquid stock at the open
instrument: stocks (ASX small/mid caps; concept applies to US)
horizon: intraday (minutes-hours); guest wants to hold >= 1 hour on A+ cases
time_of_day: open (first 30-60 min, where ~70-80% of his P&L comes)
universe_filter: Stock with fresh negative company-specific news (disappointing feasibility study, profit downgrade, bad guidance); relatively illiquid so holders need days to exit
conditions: Material negative news before the open
Thin liquidity relative to holder base
Order book shows sellers dominating at the open auction
entry_trigger: Short at/after the opening match when sellers dominate
stop: Exit immediately if the trade goes against you (mental stop; out as soon as it is red)
target_or_exit: Guest covered after 20-35 minutes but notes the move continued for hours/days; plan to hold A+ setups at least an hour and reassess
management: Size by liquidity: want resting size in the book at least as large as the position for protection; all-in/all-out
stated_edge: Forced, slow selling by holders in an illiquid name creates persistent downside drift after bad news
stated_stats: Examples: 88c open -> ~70c close same day; profit-downgrade short $8.30 covered ~$7.90 while stock reached ~$7.05
data_needed: News catalyst flag (negative company news); liquidity/ADV available
mcf_translation: Proxy without news feed: gap down <= -5% with rvol >= 3 in first 15 min and ADV below a liquidity threshold; short at 9:45 if price < VWAP and < opening 15-min low; stop above opening-range high; exit at 11:00 vs at close to test holding time.

setup_name: Overnight commodity/sector ETF read-through to local stocks at the open
instrument: stocks (resource stocks vs US-listed commodity ETFs)
universe_filter: Stocks tied to a commodity or sector whose ETF moved strongly overnight (e.g. copper ETF +5%, lithium ETF sharply down)
conditions: Related ETF/commodity moved a lot overnight
Local stock's indicated open has NOT already priced in more than the ETF move (avoid if stock gaps more than the ETF)
Pre-open book shows buyers (or sellers) rushing in
entry_trigger: Trade in the direction of the overnight ETF move at the open if order flow agrees
stop: Out as soon as it goes against you
target_or_exit: Scalp, 10-20 min typical hold
management: Skip if the stock's gap already exceeds the driver's move
stated_edge: Local stocks lag the overnight move in their driver; under-reacting gaps catch up
data_needed: Mapping of stocks to driver ETFs; US equivalent would use futures/ETF moves vs stock gap
mcf_translation: US analog: for stocks with high beta to a sector/commodity ETF (estimated on daily bars), compute expected gap = beta * ETF overnight return; if actual gap is < 50% of expected and same sign, enter at 9:35 in ETF direction; stop at opening 5-min extreme; exit at 10:30.

setup_name: Later-session VWAP-extension fade ('wallet padders')
time_of_day: after the first hour (late morning to afternoon)
universe_filter: Stocks in play that are stretched far from VWAP
conditions: Price is far above (or below) VWAP after a catalyst move
Evidence that flow is turning (not on the 'front side' while momentum still strong)
entry_trigger: Fade back toward VWAP once order flow shows the move stalling
stop: Out quickly if it keeps extending; re-try later if it extends further
target_or_exit: VWAP
management: Smaller size than morning catalyst trades
stated_edge: Overextended intraday moves mean-revert toward VWAP once the catalyst flow fades
mcf_translation: After 11:00, if 5-min close is > 2.5 ATR(5-min) above VWAP and the next bar makes a lower high, short; stop above the extreme; target VWAP; time stop at 15:30. Mirror for longs.

firm_or_style: event-driven trader (ex First New York / Apex; own family office)
setup_name: Pre-merger arbitrage: buy below a likely floor bid
universe_filter: Takeover targets with a public bid or credible press report; large holder/activist pressing for a sale; regulatory approval likely
conditions: Public bid at price P exists (or strong leak) and target board resists
Pressure (e.g. dominant shareholder) makes a deal at >= P highly likely
Stock trades below P by a margin that compensates for time and break risk
entry_trigger: Buy each time the stock trades sufficiently below the expected deal price (example: buy under 41 against a 42 bid)
stop: Exit if deal probability drops (regulatory block, buyer walks); beware sunk-cost attachment
target_or_exit: Deal consummation or bump (example closed ~43.50)
management: Assess time to close, cash vs stock, foreign approvals, whether stock ran up into the leak
stated_edge: Asymmetric payoff when deal certainty is high and the market discount is too wide
data_needed: M&A announcement/bid data, deal terms, news feed
mcf_translation: Not testable without an M&A event database. A crude MCF filter is to exclude stocks with merger-pinned price action (very low realised vol after a gap) from intraday momentum setups.

firm_or_style: independent options trader (formerly ran a small fund)
setup_name: Regime switch: buy directional options only in high-momentum/high-range markets, otherwise sell OTM premium
instrument: options on high-beta large caps and SPX/SPY (AMZN, NFLX, TSLA, NVDA, AAPL, GOOG etc.)
universe_filter: Liquid, high-beta large caps with thick option books
conditions: Momentum regime: index and names showing very large daily ranges (e.g. 75-100 point days in AMZN) -> directional long options
Quiet/chop regime -> sell far OTM options (weekly), hedging with long options/stock if a directional move starts
Signals of a coming move in a short option (volume, market-maker behaviour) prompt flipping to a directional long
entry_trigger: Long options when tape confirms momentum; exit immediately if no move ('if it isn't moving when I need it to, I'm out')
stop: Time/momentum stop on longs; hedge rather than stop on shorts
target_or_exit: Book long-option gains on the directional burst, then re-establish short premium
management: Core swing position with weekly calls sold against it while range-bound; mix moved from ~95% long options to ~60% short/40% long to reduce P&L volatility
stated_edge: Long options decay in chop; only momentum regimes pay for them. Short premium earns in quiet regimes if hedged
stated_stats: Previously monthly swings of roughly +$1M / -$0.5M; new mix described as much smoother (no numbers)
data_needed: Options chain/IV history for the options version
mcf_translation: Stock analog as a regime gate: trade intraday directional breakout setups only when SPY 5-day average true range is in the top tercile of its 1-year history (or VIX elevated); in low-range regimes trade only mean-reversion/fade setups. Test by splitting existing MCF setup results by ATR regime.

firm_or_style: prop futures trader (Genesis), runs Minter Capital trainee desk
setup_name: Inventory trading of bank-bill butterflies within their historical range
instrument: futures (ASX 90-day bank bill strip; AU 3y/10y bonds at roll)
time_of_day: day session; roll weeks for bonds
universe_filter: First 8 quarterly bank-bill contracts; butterflies/spreads with a stable historical range
conditions: Butterfly trades at the edge of its long-run range (e.g. +1 in a range of roughly -1 to +1)
Structure can be legged with little outright risk (often at market bid/offer)
entry_trigger: Accumulate the structure at the range extreme (e.g. sell butterflies at +1), legging outrights briefly then hedging with another contract
stop: No hard stop; if wrong on an outright leg, hedge with a different contract to buy time; main risk is a curve inflection/repricing
target_or_exit: Exit when the opposite range extreme is available (e.g. buy back at -1), sometimes directly at market
management: Max inventory when the opportunity is easy; avoid hard-to-leg trades
stated_edge: Highly correlated contracts on the same curve give natural hedges; patient inventory captures range mean reversion with little outright exposure
data_needed: Interest-rate futures strip data
mcf_translation: Not mappable. Closest equity analog: range-bound ETF pair spreads (e.g. sector vs SPY) traded at historical z-score extremes on daily bars.

setup_name: Cross-product order-book pressure momentum (seconds-horizon)
instrument: futures and options (KOSPI options, Japanese futures, CME options)
universe_filter: Liquid futures/options with highly correlated related products
conditions: Order-book pressure (bid/ask imbalance, sweeps, cancels) in the product and in correlated products
ML model forecasts a few-tick move over ~10 s to minutes
entry_trigger: Take liquidity in the direction of the forecast (e.g. buy high-delta options or futures as the underlying upticks)
stop: Model/hedge driven
target_or_exit: Exit after seconds to minutes; hedge horizon tuned to forecast horizon given fees
management: Many small bets across many products; liquidity-taking signals also used to defend market-making quotes
stated_edge: Speed (FPGA pre-built orders) plus microstructure signals; common signals make it a latency race
stated_stats: Was ~3-5% of volume in major index products and 10-25% in some smaller KRX/SGX products; profitable after costs in the first month
data_needed: Tick-level order book data, co-location, very low fees
mcf_translation: Not mappable to 5-min bars. Only portable idea: lead-lag between correlated instruments (e.g. ES futures/SPY leading single stocks) at the 1-5 minute scale.

setup_name: Small-cap gap-up fade inside the statistical 'money box'
time_of_day: open to noon; largest size around 9:45, mostly flat by 12:00
universe_filter: Pre-market gappers with float < 100M (often < 20M), small market cap; weak catalyst (recycled or fluffy PR, licensing 'with Walmart'-type headlines); filings show likely dilution (warrants, shelf/secondary)
conditions: Stock gaps up on low-quality news
Price rips further after the open into the 'money box': the historical range of % gain from the open (mean +/- 1 SD) and time window in which similar setups top
Daily-chart resistance and/or warrant/offering prices near the zone
Tape shows the move stalling (no fresh aggressive buyers)
entry_trigger: Short a starter (about 1/4 size) inside the money box; add as it rolls over (hit large bids) and on re-tests of the high
stop: Fixed dollar risk per trade; stop out beyond that (biggest losses came from being stubborn)
target_or_exit: Cover partials into sharp washouts (e.g. 1/4 per big red candle), re-short bounces, ride a core position toward the open/gap fill; second 'money box' marks typical bottom % and time
management: Split into a scalp portion and a core portion; size up when more factors align (stats, filings, technicals, tape); stand aside if volume forecast signals unusual demand
stated_edge: Low-quality small-cap gaps attract naive buyers and dilution-motivated pumping; the size and timing of the opening spike are statistically repeatable
stated_stats: Guest says the money box range is 'surprisingly repeatable' (no numbers); used as an alert, not a blind entry
data_needed: Float and filings (dilution) data would sharpen the filter
mcf_translation: Universe: gap >= +20% (try 10/20/40), price $1-20, pre-market/first-15-min rvol high. From history, compute distribution of (high-of-day - open)/open and the bar time of HOD for this setup. Live: when price is within [mean-1SD, mean+1SD] of the open-to-HOD % and within the typical time window, and a 5-min bar closes below prior bar low, short 1/4; add on a lower high; stop above HOD+buffer; cover 1/4 at each -1 ATR, remainder at noon or gap 50% fill. Strictly walk-forward the box parameters.

setup_name: Intraday end-of-day volume forecast as a squeeze warning
universe_filter: Stocks in play / gappers being considered for a fade
conditions: At each checkpoint, project full-day volume from cumulative volume using the stock's typical intraday volume curve
Forecast rising between checkpoints (e.g. 10M -> 11M -> 14M) = unusual demand
entry_trigger: Rising forecast after a spike-and-hold = do not short / consider long for a squeeze; flat or falling forecast supports the fade
stop: n/a (filter)
target_or_exit: n/a
management: Used as a filter on fade entries
stated_edge: Deviations from the normal intraday volume distribution reveal hidden buying that holds price up and later squeezes it
stated_stats: New tool still being tested (credited idea to @alldayfaders)
mcf_translation: Build per-stock (or per-bucket) cumulative-volume share curve by 5-min bar from history. Forecast EOD vol = cumvol(t)/share(t). Feature = forecast(t)/forecast(t-2 bars). Test: for gap-fade candidates, compare fade P&L when feature > 1.2 vs < 1.0; and test long breakout when feature rising and price holds above VWAP.

setup_name: SSR-day short via midpoint/dark-pool fills
universe_filter: Stocks under SSR (down >= 10% today or yesterday)
conditions: Stock tightens into a narrow range
Offers start stacking and bids pull (chain reaction)
entry_trigger: Short at the midpoint across many venues/dark pools ahead of shorts stuck on the offer
stop: Cover if the stacked offer gets lifted
target_or_exit: 5-35 cent moves
management: Scalp; edge faded in 2018 as offers became less reliable (spoofing)
stated_edge: Routing access lets you get short when others cannot hit the bid
data_needed: Level 2, venue routing, SSR status; fills at midpoint not modelable with bars
mcf_translation: Bars can only test the directional part: on day 2 of SSR (prior day -10%+), short a break of the first-30-min range low with stop at range high; exit at close.

firm_or_style: prop futures click trader with systematic rules
setup_name: Beta-weighted correlated-index spread fade at standard-deviation bands
instrument: futures (ASX SPI vs E-mini S&P, Nikkei, DAX; AU 3y vs 10y bonds; US 10y/ultra/30y)
time_of_day: mainly the overnight/US session for AU trader
universe_filter: Pairs of highly correlated index or bond futures
conditions: Hedge ratio from regression of returns (30-min/hourly data) and equal dollar-per-1% sizing
Spread deviates a set number of standard deviations from its mean
entry_trigger: Fade the spread at the SD band (scale in at further bands)
stop: Stop at a deeper SD level defined in testing; avoid discretionary early exits not in the test
target_or_exit: Partial revert or back to the mean; in high-volatility regimes the moves run further (reward/risk improved from ~1:1 to ~1.5:1+)
management: Tilt the ratio (e.g. 4:3) when holding an outright view; cut size on the subset of trades that tests show carry more risk; avoid holding through bond roll weeks
stated_edge: Correlated markets dislocate temporarily on flows (late-session lack of flow, big players executing) and revert
stated_stats: Live results checked weekly against tested expectations; ~80% of tested payoff is the profitability benchmark; one 6-figure drawdown over ~5 weeks recovered in about a month
data_needed: Futures data for the original; ETF pairs possible
mcf_translation: ETF analog on 5-min bars: spread = log(QQQ) - b*log(SPY) (also IWM/SPY, XLK/SPY, EWA or EWJ vs SPY in US hours) with b from rolling 20-day regression of 30-min returns; z-score vs rolling 5-day mean; enter at |z|>2, add at 2.5, stop at 3.5, exit at z=0.5 or close. Costs on both legs.

setup_name: IPO day-one fade when price cannot reclaim the opening print
time_of_day: from the IPO open through the session
universe_filter: First trading day of a heavily hyped IPO priced repeatedly higher pre-listing; very high volume (e.g. a third of the float in 5 minutes); shares locatable
conditions: Opening print used as the reference level
Price drops below the open, bounces but fails to get back above it
Price trades below the high-volume node (volume profile) so most buyers are underwater
Large bids at round dollars get traded through
entry_trigger: Starter short (1/4-1/2 size) once the bounce fails below the open; add only as new lower highs confirm (add to winners, never losers)
stop: Above the opening print/high (if it reclaims and makes highs, take the starter loss)
target_or_exit: Cover about half at each big round-number bid (e.g. 86, 83, 80) and re-short bounces to the prior round number; if bounces stop reaching re-short levels, cover passively only at the next big figure; exit the rest when price makes a higher high above a recent bounce high
management: Trade around a core; resting cover orders with iceberg size at round numbers; flat by close
stated_edge: Over-hyped IPO pricing leaves more supply than demand; trapped buyers sell into bounces; round-number bids act as temporary support
stated_stats: Lyft example: open ~88, covered most at 80 (about -9%); first short produced ~2/3 of day P&L
data_needed: IPO calendar/first-trade-day flag (can infer from first bar in data), float
mcf_translation: Universe: first trading day (first available bar) with market cap > $1B. Reference = first 5-min open. Short when a 5-min bar closes below the opening price after a bounce that fails to close above it; stop above day high; cover 1/2 at -5% and rest at close or on a 5-min close above the last swing high. Compare with mirrored long rule for IPOs holding above open.

setup_name: Large round-number bid: lean long on first test, short the break on later tests
universe_filter: Very active stocks with a visible large resting bid at a whole-dollar level
conditions: Big round-number bid holds on the first test after a decline (momentum fading, chop)
Later tests: bid size shrinks (e.g. 500k -> 300k) and bounces get weaker (lower highs)
entry_trigger: Long near the level on the first retest with risk of tens of cents; later, short as the shrinking bid is about to be taken out
stop: Long: below the level / below the prior swing low; Short: above the last bounce high (e.g. back over 81)
target_or_exit: Long: a few dollars or failure back through recent low; Short: quick flush with resting cover orders 1-2 dollars below
management: If the break short does not work immediately, cut half at once
stated_edge: Everyone watches the same big bid; its removal triggers a waterfall of exiting longs
data_needed: Level 2 bid size for the full version
mcf_translation: Bar proxy: whole-dollar level L with at least 2 touches (5-min lows within 0.2% of L). On a third touch where each bounce high is lower, short a 5-min close below L - 0.1%; stop above last bounce high; target 1.5x the bounce height; flat at close.

setup_name: Strong-IPO continuation long (day 1-2)
universe_filter: New IPOs that hold or extend their first-day prices
conditions: IPO holds its opening price or drifts higher on day 1
No layer of trapped buyers overhead (all holders in profit)
entry_trigger: Buy day 1-2 as it holds/extends above first-day range
stop: Below the first-day hold level
target_or_exit: Ride while it keeps making highs
management: Not detailed
stated_edge: With no underwater holders there is no overhead supply; open-ended upside
stated_stats: Examples cited: TWLO, TLRY
data_needed: IPO first-day flag
mcf_translation: Day 2 of listing: if day 1 closed above its open and in top 30% of range, buy day 2 on break of day 1 high; stop below day 1 low or VWAP; hold up to 5 days.

setup_name: Panic-flush reversal (capitulation bounce) in liquid stocks
instrument: US stocks (large caps e.g. FANG names; also low floats)
time_of_day: any; best in high-VIX, panicky markets
universe_filter: Liquid names selling off on panic/flows, NOT on fresh company news; elevated VIX regime
conditions: Fast, steep intraday drop (slope criterion)
Volume rising steadily into the drop
No stock-specific negative news
entry_trigger: Buy the first green bar after the climactic, high-volume flush (full size when criteria met)
stop: Fixed stop (example risk ~35 cents)
target_or_exit: Quick 25-60 cents (example target ~55-60c vs 35c risk)
management: Algorithmic alerts flag slope+volume conditions; discretionary filter on whether it is noise; trade only when volatility is high
stated_edge: Panic selling overshoots in non-news selloffs; volume climax marks exhaustion
stated_stats: Reward/risk roughly 1.6:1 per the example; no win rate
data_needed: News flag to exclude news-driven drops
mcf_translation: On 5-min bars: price down >= 3 ATR(5-min) over last 6 bars, each of last 3 bars with volume above prior bar and rvol > 3; enter long at close of first green bar; stop below flush low; target 1.5R or VWAP; only when VIX > 20 (or SPY 10-day realised vol in top tercile). Exclude stocks with overnight gap > 5% (likely news).

setup_name: Market-on-close imbalance offset
time_of_day: from 15:50 ET imbalance publication to the closing print; best on index rebalance days (Russell reconstitution, quad witching, S&P rebalances)
universe_filter: Stocks with large published closing imbalances relative to volume
conditions: Large published imbalance (e.g. sell imbalance) and indicative clearing price far from the last trade
Imbalance not offset by other participants
entry_trigger: Take the opposite side in the continuous market (e.g. short now) and enter a matching market-on-close order on the imbalance side (buy MOC), capturing the gap between pre-close price and closing print
stop: Risk: imbalances cancelled at the last minute (manipulation) or fill not received
target_or_exit: Flat at the closing print
management: Watch updated clearing-price feed; larger edges on volatile days
stated_edge: Forced institutional closing flows push the closing price away from fair value
stated_stats: Edge shrank from 35-50 cents per share (2008) to a few cents normally
data_needed: Closing-auction imbalance feeds and closing prints
mcf_translation: Partial proxy: on known rebalance dates, test 15:50-close return vs 16:00-next open reversal for stocks with abnormal last-10-min volume; needs exchange imbalance data for a real test.

firm_or_style: crypto quant trading firm (Alameda Research), ex-Jane Street ETF trader
setup_name: Absorb a large seller on one venue, hedge on other venues (cross-venue liquidity arbitrage)
instrument: crypto (BTC, ETH etc. across ~30 exchanges; futures for hedging)
universe_filter: Assets where one venue's price is dislocated by concentrated one-sided customer flow
conditions: A venue trades a few % away from the rest of the market due to a large seller/buyer
Capital and inventory pre-positioned on the relevant venues
entry_trigger: Buy the dislocated venue's offer once it is cheap enough versus other venues
stop: Position limits sized so a worst case cannot threaten the firm
target_or_exit: Simultaneously sell/short on other venues or futures; never sell back on the same depressed venue
management: Automated execution with human-set parameters (position limits, required edge, quote size, capital placement); limit assets left on any single exchange (hack risk)
stated_edge: Fragmented capital and operational barriers (withdrawal limits, banking, stablecoin redemption) keep arbitrages alive for those who solve the plumbing
stated_stats: Claimed ~$1B/day turnover, ~5% of global crypto volume (2019 claims; firm later collapsed in the FTX fraud case)
data_needed: Multi-venue crypto order books and transfer constraints
mcf_translation: Not mappable to MCF.

firm_or_style: systematic trend follower / author (weekly breakout momentum on stocks)
setup_name: Weekly 20-week-high breakout with ROC filter and index regime gate
time_of_day: signals on weekly close; orders executed at next open
universe_filter: Historical index constituents (survivorship-free); 50-day average volume so an order is at most ~2-3% of ADV
conditions: Broad index above its 200-day moving average (regime filter)
Weekly close at a 20-week high
20-week rate of change above ~30%
If more signals than free slots, rank by rate of change
entry_trigger: Buy at next open after a qualifying weekly close
stop: 20% trailing stop on closing prices; tightened to ~10% when the regime filter turns bearish
target_or_exit: Exit next open after a close below the trailing stop; no profit target, no time stop
management: 20 equal-weight positions of ~5% each (volatility weighting added little in his tests)
stated_edge: Momentum leaders keep trending; regime filter avoids bear-market drawdowns; letting winners run produces a large payoff ratio
stated_stats: Roughly 44% win rate, average win ~31% vs average loss ~12%, average loss ~0.6% of portfolio; regime filter roughly halved max drawdown (~48% to ~24%) in his tests
data_needed: Daily bars resampled to weekly; index constituent history ideally; index 200-day MA
mcf_translation: Daily-bar lab: weekly close = Friday close; signal = 20-week high & 20w ROC > 30% & SPY > SMA200; next-open entry; 20% close-based trailing stop (10% when SPY < SMA200); 20 slots ranked by ROC; costs included.

setup_name: Relative momentum rotation (top-N by rate of change, monthly rebalance)
universe_filter: Index constituents such as the Nasdaq 100
conditions: Rank universe by rate of change over a lookback
Optional index regime filter (index above long MA)
entry_trigger: Hold the top N ranked names at each monthly rebalance
stop: None besides dropping out of the top ranks (or regime filter turning off)
target_or_exit: Sell names that fall out of the top N at rebalance
management: Equal weight across N holdings
stated_edge: Cross-sectional momentum persists
stated_stats: None given
data_needed: Daily bars for universe; constituent history
mcf_translation: Monthly ROC ranking on the MCF universe, top N equal weight, SPY>SMA200 gate, costs in.

firm_or_style: prop day trader (7 Points Capital), short-only low-float micro-cap specialist
setup_name: Short the turn in an overextended micro-cap runner, entering on stop-triggered breakdown
horizon: intraday (scalp to several hours); sometimes day 2
time_of_day: any; often after the morning push fails; regime decides day 1 open vs day 2
universe_filter: Low-float micro caps with big percentage gap/run on news or PR, heavy volume
conditions: Stock heavily extended after a multi-hour or multi-day run
Wait for clear shift: buyers who accumulated all day likely to start selling (failed push / sharp reversal)
Micro-cap regime check: in strong micro markets avoid day 1 and look for day-2 opportunities; in weak micro markets be more aggressive fading off the open
Avoid entering where every other short has the same obvious stop
entry_trigger: Use stop orders to 'slip into' the short as price breaks down, adding only as price moves in his favour
stop: Hard stops (several staggered levels), tight collar when sized up; firm daily loss lockout
target_or_exit: Decide early if it is a scalp or a fade-all-day position; cover into flushes where trapped longs' stops trigger
management: Add size only with price; scale size incrementally after success and cut size in drawdowns; never add against a position
stated_edge: Patience to stay uninvolved until the turn gives a clear head and allows full size at the inflection; trapped longs' stops fuel the move
stated_stats: None given
data_needed: 5-min bars, float, news catalyst flags, borrow availability
mcf_translation: Proxy: small caps (price < $20) up > 50% intraday or prior day with rvol > 5; short on 5-min close below prior bar low after a failed new high, stop above HOD; exit EOD or at VWAP; compare day-1 vs day-2 entries and condition on recent small-cap runner follow-through (regime).

setup_name: Short a stock with a persistent large seller despite a strong related commodity/driver (relative weakness)
instrument: ASX equities (example: iron ore miner vs iron ore price); translatable to US stocks vs sector/commodity ETF
time_of_day: throughout session; enter after each bounce is sold
universe_filter: Liquid mid caps with a catalyst/in-play status and a clear external driver
conditions: Related driver (commodity or sector) trending up for days
Stock fails to follow and keeps getting sold into on each bounce
Bounces only manage a few ticks before heavy selling reappears
entry_trigger: Short when a bounce is met again by large selling (bids refill then get hit)
stop: Above the bounce high / when the seller disappears
target_or_exit: Scalp back to the intraday lows or nearby round number; do not hold long once the seller is gone
management: Do not fight it with long bias; avoid adding to losers
stated_edge: Large institutional sellers must work orders over days; their footprint shows as repeated selling into strength
stated_stats: None (one loss of ~$4.5k came from ignoring this signal on the long side)
data_needed: 5-min bars for stock and related ETF/commodity proxy; tape/order flow not available
mcf_translation: Daily screen: stock down N days while its sector/commodity ETF up (negative residual vs ETF beta). Intraday: short failed bounces below VWAP (bounce < 0.5 ATR then new 5-min low), exit EOD; measure next-day continuation of residual weakness.

setup_name: Round-number break scalp in low-priced in-play stocks
instrument: low-priced ASX small/mid caps (US analog: sub-$10 stocks)
universe_filter: Low-denomination stocks with a news catalyst so per-share commission drag is small relative to moves
conditions: Stock in play on catalyst
Approaching a round number (e.g. $1.00)
entry_trigger: Buy the push through the round number
stop: Back below the level
target_or_exit: Take a quick few-percent spike if no follow-through (bids stepped in) rather than holding
management: Trade around the position several times; track commission as % of profit per trade
stated_edge: Order flow around round numbers; low-priced stocks give larger % moves relative to fixed bps commission
stated_stats: None given; notes 20 bps round-trip commission kills small scalps on higher-priced stocks
data_needed: 5-min bars (1-min better), catalyst flag
mcf_translation: Low-price (<$10) gappers crossing a whole-dollar level on 5-min close; exit after 2-3 bars or on close back below the level; include realistic costs.

guest: Dan Shapiro (clip from ep66, in Best of Risk Management Pt.1)
firm_or_style: independent equities trader, ex-NYC prop; high-beta names
setup_name: Prior-day-high breakout with stop at prior close and fixed 1% risk sizing
time_of_day: next session after the setup day; trigger whenever price takes out prior high
universe_filter: Stocks that closed near (just below) the prior day's high
conditions: Prior close near the day's high (small gap between close and high)
Homework done the night before on daily charts
entry_trigger: Buy stop at prior day's high
stop: Prior day's close (or a 15-min chart level); risk per trade fixed at ~1% of account
target_or_exit: Take partial profit into strength, hold a runner, move stop to breakeven
management: Shares = (1% of equity) / (entry - stop); tighter close-to-high distance gives larger size; avoid holding biotechs overnight
stated_edge: Fixed max pain removes emotion; tight risk to prior close gives large reward-to-risk on multi-day runs
stated_stats: None given
data_needed: Daily bars (prior high/close) and 5-min bars for intraday trigger and stop
mcf_translation: Filter: (prior high - prior close)/ATR < 0.2. Entry: first 5-min bar trading above prior high. Stop: prior close. Exit: half at +2R, rest on breakeven stop or EOD/N-day hold. Size by fixed 1% risk; costs in; compare intraday vs 3-day hold.
